# Command Console contract

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-contract.mjs. Do not edit: change packages/command-console/src/contract.ts, the component, contract/rules.md or contract/dom.ts and run `pnpm contract:gen`. -->

This is the public contract of `@dolusoft/command-console`: the component surface, the types, the behavior rules and the DOM the component renders. A check or a test is tied to each part; see the end of this file. A behavior rule is traced when a test names its ID. That shows every rule has a test, not that the test covers the rule: traceability is not coverage.

## Component

### Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `commands` | `CommandDefinition[]` | yes |  | The commands; validated on every change (C-56). |
| `prompt` | `string` |  | `undefined` | The root prompt. Default `'>'`. |
| `initialState` | `Partial<ControllableState>` |  | `undefined` | The first value of each uncontrolled slice; read once. |
| `createId` | `(() => string)` |  | `undefined` | Makes entry and run ids. Default: a per-console counter. |
| `maxEntries` | `number` |  | `undefined` | Drops the oldest entries beyond this. Default unbounded. |
| `beforeRun` | `((info: RunInfo, signal: AbortSignal) => BeforeRunResult \| Promise<BeforeRunResult>)` |  | `undefined` | Called when a command is about to run (permission checks, C-14). |
| `onError` | `((error: unknown, info: RunInfo \| null) => void)` |  | `undefined` | A command threw (`info` set) or a callback threw (`info` null). Receives the error exactly as it was thrown. |
| `formatError` | `((error: unknown, info: RunInfo) => CommandResponse)` |  | `undefined` | Turns a command's error into its output. Default `command-failed`. |
| `isSensitive` | `((line: string) => boolean)` |  | `undefined` | Marks more lines sensitive, OR-ed with the commands' `sensitive`. |
| `recallLimit` | `number` |  | `undefined` | The most lines recall keeps. Default 100. |
| `shouldRecord` | `((line: string) => boolean)` |  | `undefined` | Whether a submitted line is recorded for recall. Default every line. |
| `labels` | `ConsoleLabelsInput` |  | `undefined` | Texts over the English defaults (C-47). |
| `autofocus` | `boolean` |  | `false` | Focuses the input on mount (C-51). Default `false`. |
| `entries` | `ConsoleEntry[]` |  | `undefined` | The entries, for `v-model:entries`; controlled when bound (C-04). |
| `recall` | `string[]` |  | `undefined` | The recall list, for `v-model:recall`; controlled when bound. |
| `context` | `ContextFrame[]` |  | `undefined` | The context frames, for `v-model:context`; controlled when bound. |

### Events

| Name | Arguments | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `update:entries` | `[entries: ConsoleEntry[]]` | The new entries of a bound `v-model:entries`, resolved against the last emitted value (C-61). |
| `update:recall` | `[recall: string[]]` | The new recall list of a bound `v-model:recall`. |
| `update:context` | `[context: ContextFrame[]]` | The new context frames of a bound `v-model:context`. |
| `close` | `[]` | A command returned the `close` effect (C-25). |
| `submit` | `[submit: ConsoleSubmit]` | A line was submitted with Enter or the exposed `run` (C-64). |

### Slots

| Name | Props | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `block-text` | `BlockSlotProps<TextBlock>` | Replaces the rendering of a text block. |
| `block-json` | `BlockSlotProps<JsonBlock>` | Replaces the rendering of a JSON block (for example to highlight it). |
| `block-table` | `BlockSlotProps<TableBlock>` | Replaces the rendering of a table block. |
| `block-list` | `BlockSlotProps<ListBlock>` | Replaces the rendering of a list block. |
| `block-message` | `BlockSlotProps<MessageBlock>` | Replaces the rendering of a message block. |
| `block-custom` | `BlockSlotProps<CustomBlock>` | Renders a custom block; without it the block shows as JSON. |
| `prompt` | `{ prompt: string }` | Inside each `span.cc-prompt`. |
| `busy` | `{ running: RunningCommand }` | Inside `.cc-status` while a command runs. |
| `completion` | `CompletionSlotProps` | Inside each `li.cc-completion`. |

### Exposed

| Name | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `focus` | `() => void` | Focuses the input. |
| `run` | `(line: string) => Promise<boolean>` | Replaces the input with `line` and submits it, as the user would (C-63); keeps the log at the bottom. |
| `cancel` | `() => void` | Interrupts the running command, else cancels the line. |
| `reset` | `() => void` | Ends the run and returns every slice to its initial value. |
| `clear` | `() => void` | Removes every entry. |
| `console` | `Console<OptionalFeatures>` | The console, with every optional feature. |
| `state` | `ConsoleState` | The console's state (for example `running`, to key an overlay on). A template ref unwraps it: reading it in a computed or a template tracks it. |

### Functions

Exported from the package entry point next to the component.

| Name | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `useCommandConsole` | `(options: UseCommandConsoleOptions<T>) => UseCommandConsoleReturn<T>` | Creates a console from `options` and keeps it in step with them. A value option (`commands`, `prompt`, `state`, `maxEntries`, `recallLimit`) may be a plain value, a ref or a getter. A function option (`beforeRun`, `onError`, …) may be the function or a ref that holds it: a bare function is the option itself, never a getter. `features` and `initialState` are read once. |

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Labels (README: Labels, P7)

/** The text of one message code: a string, or a function of its parameters. */
export type MessageLabels = {
  [C in MessageCode]: string | ((params: MessageParams[C]) => string)
}

/** Every text the component renders (C-47). */
export interface ConsoleLabels {
  /** The input's accessible name. Default `'Command'`. */
  input: string
  /**
   * The input's description (`aria-description`): how Enter and Tab behave,
   * and that Tab on an empty line leaves the console (C-59).
   */
  inputDescription: string
  /** The log's accessible name. Default `'Console output'`. */
  log: string
  /** Shown instead of a sensitive line. Default `'(input hidden)'`. */
  redacted: string
  /** Shown after a line ended with Ctrl+C. Default `'^C'`. */
  cancelledMarker: string
  /** The completion list's accessible name. Default `'Suggestions'`. */
  completions: string
  /** The status text while a command runs. Default `'Running…'`. */
  busy: string
  /** The text of each library-made message block. */
  messages: MessageLabels
}

/**
 * The `labels` prop: any part of `ConsoleLabels`. `messages` is merged one
 * level deep, so overriding one message keeps the others.
 */
export type ConsoleLabelsInput = Partial<Omit<ConsoleLabels, 'messages'>> & {
  messages?: Partial<MessageLabels>
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The component

/** The props of `<CommandConsole>`. */
export interface ConsoleProps {
  /** The commands; validated on every change (C-56). */
  commands: CommandDefinition[]
  /** The root prompt. Default `'>'`. */
  prompt?: string
  /** The first value of each uncontrolled slice; read once. */
  initialState?: Partial<ControllableState>
  /** Makes entry and run ids. Default: a per-console counter. */
  createId?: () => string
  /** Drops the oldest entries beyond this. Default unbounded. */
  maxEntries?: number
  /** Called when a command is about to run (permission checks, C-14). */
  beforeRun?: (
    info: RunInfo,
    signal: AbortSignal
  ) => BeforeRunResult | Promise<BeforeRunResult>
  /**
   * A command threw (`info` set) or a callback threw (`info` null). Receives
   * the error exactly as it was thrown.
   */
  onError?: (error: unknown, info: RunInfo | null) => void
  /** Turns a command's error into its output. Default `command-failed`. */
  formatError?: (error: unknown, info: RunInfo) => CommandResponse
  /** Marks more lines sensitive, OR-ed with the commands' `sensitive`. */
  isSensitive?: (line: string) => boolean
  /** The most lines recall keeps. Default 100. */
  recallLimit?: number
  /** Whether a submitted line is recorded for recall. Default every line. */
  shouldRecord?: (line: string) => boolean
  /** Texts over the English defaults (C-47). */
  labels?: ConsoleLabelsInput
  /** Focuses the input on mount (C-51). Default `false`. */
  autofocus?: boolean
  /** The entries, for `v-model:entries`; controlled when bound (C-04). */
  entries?: ConsoleEntry[]
  /** The recall list, for `v-model:recall`; controlled when bound. */
  recall?: string[]
  /** The context frames, for `v-model:context`; controlled when bound. */
  context?: ContextFrame[]
}

/** What the `submit` event carries: never the line (C-64). */
export interface ConsoleSubmit {
  /** The id of the input entry the line ended as. */
  inputId: string
  /** Whether the line was sensitive and its entry redacted. */
  sensitive: boolean
}

/** The events of `<CommandConsole>`. */
export interface ConsoleEmits {
  /**
   * The new entries of a bound `v-model:entries`, resolved against the last
   * emitted value (C-61).
   */
  'update:entries': [entries: ConsoleEntry[]]
  /** The new recall list of a bound `v-model:recall`. */
  'update:recall': [recall: string[]]
  /** The new context frames of a bound `v-model:context`. */
  'update:context': [context: ContextFrame[]]
  /** A command returned the `close` effect (C-25). */
  close: []
  /** A line was submitted with Enter or the exposed `run` (C-64). */
  submit: [submit: ConsoleSubmit]
}

/** What a `block-<type>` slot receives. */
export interface BlockSlotProps<B extends OutputBlock = OutputBlock> {
  block: B
  entry: OutputEntry
}

/** What the `completion` slot receives. */
export interface CompletionSlotProps {
  candidate: string
  index: number
  /** Whether this candidate is the selected one. */
  active: boolean
}

/** The slots of `<CommandConsole>` (C-67). */
export interface ConsoleSlots {
  /** Replaces the rendering of a text block. */
  'block-text'?(props: BlockSlotProps<TextBlock>): unknown
  /** Replaces the rendering of a JSON block (for example to highlight it). */
  'block-json'?(props: BlockSlotProps<JsonBlock>): unknown
  /** Replaces the rendering of a table block. */
  'block-table'?(props: BlockSlotProps<TableBlock>): unknown
  /** Replaces the rendering of a list block. */
  'block-list'?(props: BlockSlotProps<ListBlock>): unknown
  /** Replaces the rendering of a message block. */
  'block-message'?(props: BlockSlotProps<MessageBlock>): unknown
  /** Renders a custom block; without it the block shows as JSON. */
  'block-custom'?(props: BlockSlotProps<CustomBlock>): unknown
  /** Inside each `span.cc-prompt`. */
  prompt?(props: { prompt: string }): unknown
  /** Inside `.cc-status` while a command runs. */
  busy?(props: { running: RunningCommand }): unknown
  /** Inside each `li.cc-completion`. */
  completion?(props: CompletionSlotProps): unknown
}

/** What a template ref to `<CommandConsole>` reaches. */
export interface ConsoleExpose {
  /** Focuses the input. */
  focus(): void
  /**
   * Replaces the input with `line` and submits it, as the user would
   * (C-63); keeps the log at the bottom.
   */
  run(line: string): Promise<boolean>
  /** Interrupts the running command, else cancels the line. */
  cancel(): void
  /** Ends the run and returns every slice to its initial value. */
  reset(): void
  /** Removes every entry. */
  clear(): void
  /** The console, with every optional feature. */
  console: Console<OptionalFeatures>
  /**
   * The console's state (for example `running`, to key an overlay on). A
   * template ref unwraps it: reading it in a computed or a template tracks
   * it.
   */
  state: ConsoleState
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The composable

/** The value options of `useCommandConsole`: a value, a ref or a getter. */
type ValueOptions<T extends Partial<OptionalFeatures>> = {
  [K in 'prompt' | 'state' | 'maxEntries' | 'recallLimit']?: MaybeRefOrGetter<
    ConsoleOptions<T>[K]
  >
}

/** The function options of `useCommandConsole`: a function or a ref to one. */
type FunctionOptions<T extends Partial<OptionalFeatures>> = {
  [
    K in
      | 'onEntriesChange'
      | 'onRecallChange'
      | 'onContextChange'
      | 'createId'
      | 'beforeRun'
      | 'onError'
      | 'formatError'
      | 'onClose'
      | 'isSensitive'
      | 'shouldRecord'
  ]?: MaybeRef<ConsoleOptions<T>[K]>
}

/** The options of `useCommandConsole`: the core options, reactive. */
export type UseCommandConsoleOptions<
  // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-empty-object-type
  T extends Partial<OptionalFeatures> = {}
> = ValueOptions<T> &
  FunctionOptions<T> & {
    /** The optional features; fixed for the life of the console. */
    features?: T
    commands: MaybeRefOrGetter<CommandDefinition[]>
    /** Read once, when the console is created. */
    initialState?: MaybeRefOrGetter<Partial<ControllableState> | undefined>
  }

/** What `useCommandConsole` returns. */
export interface UseCommandConsoleReturn<
  // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-empty-object-type
  T extends Partial<OptionalFeatures> = {}
> {
  /** The console; disposed with the effect scope. */
  console: Console<T>
  /** The state after every action (C-68). */
  state: Readonly<ShallowRef<ConsoleState>>
}

`contract.ts` exports the types below again; they are declared by the protocol or the core.

```ts
// packages/command-protocol/src/block.ts
/** Plain text, rendered preformatted. */
export interface TextBlock {
  type: 'text'
  text: string
}

// packages/command-protocol/src/block.ts
/** A JSON value, rendered as `JSON.stringify(value, null, 2)`. */
export interface JsonBlock {
  type: 'json'
  value: JsonValue
}

// packages/command-protocol/src/block.ts
/** One column of a table block: the row key it reads and its header text. */
export interface TableColumn {
  key: string
  label: string
}

// packages/command-protocol/src/block.ts
/** A table: a header row from `columns`, then one row per `rows` item. */
export interface TableBlock {
  type: 'table'
  columns: TableColumn[]
  rows: Record<string, JsonPrimitive>[]
}

// packages/command-protocol/src/block.ts
/** A list of text items. */
export interface ListBlock {
  type: 'list'
  items: string[]
}

// packages/command-protocol/src/block.ts
/**
 * A message the library makes. It carries a code, never text: the Vue package
 * renders it from its labels (P7).
 */
export interface MessageBlock {
  type: 'message'
  code: MessageCode
  params?: Record<string, JsonPrimitive>
}

// packages/command-protocol/src/block.ts
/** A block the consumer renders itself, told apart by `kind`. */
export interface CustomBlock {
  type: 'custom'
  kind: string
  data?: JsonValue
}

// packages/command-protocol/src/block.ts
/** One piece of an output entry. Output is never HTML (ADR 0005). */
export type OutputBlock =
  TextBlock | JsonBlock | TableBlock | ListBlock | MessageBlock | CustomBlock

// packages/command-protocol/src/block.ts
/**
 * The messages the library makes:
 *
 * - `command-not-found`: the first token names no command.
 * - `command-failed`: the command threw or rejected; the error's text is never
 *   shown (S-06).
 * - `unterminated-quote`: the line has a quote that is not closed.
 * - `interrupted`: a running command was cancelled.
 */
export type MessageCode =
  'command-not-found' | 'command-failed' | 'unterminated-quote' | 'interrupted'

// packages/command-protocol/src/block.ts
/**
 * The parameters of each message code. For a sensitive line `name` and
 * `index` are `null`. A code without parameters has an empty record; its
 * block carries no `params`.
 */
export interface MessageParams {
  'command-not-found': { name: string | null }
  'command-failed': Record<string, never>
  'unterminated-quote': { index: number | null }
  interrupted: Record<string, never>
}

// packages/command-protocol/src/command.ts
/**
 * The JSON part of a command: its names and how it is listed and redacted.
 * The core adds the functions (`run`, `complete`) to it.
 */
export interface CommandSpec {
  /** Non-empty, no whitespace, no quote characters; unique with the aliases. */
  name: string
  /** Other names that run the same command; the same rules as `name`. */
  aliases?: string[]
  /** One line on what the command does, for the consumer's help. */
  summary?: string
  /** How the command is called, for the consumer's help. */
  usage?: string
  /** Not listed by `getCommands` and not completed by name. */
  hidden?: boolean
  /**
   * Arguments at and after `fromArg` are secret, so the line is redacted and
   * those positions are never completed. `true` is `{ fromArg: 0 }`.
   */
  sensitive?: boolean | { fromArg: number }
}

// packages/command-protocol/src/command.ts
/** What a command returns, as JSON. */
export interface CommandResponse {
  /** A string is one text block. */
  output?: string | OutputBlock[]
  /** Default `'default'`. */
  tone?: OutputEntry['tone']
  /** Copied to the output entry. */
  quiet?: true
  /** Applied in order, before the output is appended. */
  effects?: ConsoleEffect[]
}

// packages/command-protocol/src/command.ts
/**
 * A change a command asks the console to make:
 *
 * - `clear`: empty the entries.
 * - `close`: ask the consumer to close the console.
 * - `push-context`: push a frame on the context stack.
 * - `pop-context`: pop `count` frames (default 1); stops at the root.
 * - `reset-context`: return to the root.
 * - `clear-recall`: empty the recall list.
 */
export type ConsoleEffect =
  | { type: 'clear' }
  | { type: 'close' }
  | { type: 'push-context'; frame: ContextFrame }
  | { type: 'pop-context'; count?: number }
  | { type: 'reset-context' }
  | { type: 'clear-recall' }

// packages/command-protocol/src/context.ts
/**
 * One level of the context stack. The stack runs bottom → top; the root is
 * implicit and has no frame. The prompt of a new input entry is the top
 * frame's `prompt`. What a frame means is the consumer's (`data`).
 */
export interface ContextFrame {
  /** Identifies the frame; a change of the id sequence is a context change. */
  id: string
  /** The prompt shown while this frame is on top. */
  prompt: string
  /** The consumer's data for this frame. */
  data?: JsonValue
}

// packages/command-protocol/src/entry.ts
/** One entry of the scrollback: a line the user ended, or output. */
export type ConsoleEntry = InputEntry | OutputEntry

// packages/command-protocol/src/entry.ts
/** A line the user ended, with the prompt it was ended with. */
export interface InputEntry {
  id: string
  kind: 'input'
  /** The prompt when the line ended. */
  prompt: string
  /** The trimmed line; `null` when the line was sensitive. */
  text: string | null
  /** True when the line was sensitive and its text is not kept. */
  redacted: boolean
  /** `cancelled` when the line was ended with Ctrl+C. */
  status: 'submitted' | 'cancelled'
}

// packages/command-protocol/src/entry.ts
/** What a command or the library wrote. */
export interface OutputEntry {
  id: string
  kind: 'output'
  tone: 'default' | 'error' | 'notice'
  blocks: OutputBlock[]
  /** The input entry this output answers. */
  inputId?: string
  /** Not announced by the live region (long output such as a whole config). */
  quiet?: true
}

// packages/command-protocol/src/json.ts
/** A JSON leaf. Numbers are finite: `NaN` and the infinities are not JSON. */
export type JsonPrimitive = string | number | boolean | null

// packages/command-protocol/src/json.ts
/**
 * A JSON value: a primitive, an array of values or a plain object of values.
 * Every protocol type is made of these (P4).
 */
export type JsonValue =
  JsonPrimitive | JsonValue[] | { [key: string]: JsonValue }

// packages/command-console-core/src/core/console/console.types.ts
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// State (core README: State)

/** The live input line. */
export interface InputState {
  value: string
  /** UTF-16 offset of the caret in `value`. */
  caret: number
  /**
   * Changes when the input element must be replaced: after a sensitive line
   * ends, on `reset()` and on a programmatic clear of a non-empty input.
   */
  revision: number
}

// packages/command-console-core/src/core/console/console.types.ts
/** The command that runs now. */
export interface RunningCommand {
  runId: string
  /** The canonical name of the command. */
  command: string
  inputId: string
  /** `authorizing` while `beforeRun` has not answered. */
  phase: 'authorizing' | 'running'
}

// packages/command-console-core/src/core/console/console.types.ts
/** An open completion (completion feature, README: Completion). */
export interface CompletionSession {
  status: 'open' | 'none'
  /** Filtered, deduplicated, in the provider's order. */
  candidates: string[]
  final: boolean
  /** The selected candidate; -1 when none is. */
  active: number
  /** The token's raw span in `input.value`, updated after each write. */
  span: { start: number; end: number }
  /** The token's raw text before the session. */
  original: string
}

// packages/command-console-core/src/core/console/console.types.ts
/** Everything the console holds. */
export interface ConsoleState {
  entries: ConsoleEntry[]
  input: InputState
  running: RunningCommand | null
  /** Oldest → newest (recall feature). */
  recall: string[]
  recallCursor: number | null
  recallDraft: string | null
  completion: CompletionSession | null
  /** Bottom → top; the root is implicit (context feature). */
  context: ContextFrame[]
}

// packages/command-console-core/src/core/console/console.types.ts
/** The slices a consumer may control (core README: Controlled slices). */
export interface ControllableState {
  entries: ConsoleEntry[]
  recall: string[]
  context: ContextFrame[]
}

// packages/command-console-core/src/core/console/console.types.ts
/**
 * The optional features, by the key `options.features` takes. A console has
 * the methods of the features it was created with, in its type and at run
 * time.
 */
export interface OptionalFeatures {
  recallFeature: RecallFeature
  completionFeature: CompletionFeature
  contextFeature: ContextFeature
}

// packages/command-console-core/src/core/console/console.types.ts
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Options (core README: Options)

/** What a console is created with. */
export interface ConsoleOptions<
  // `{}` and not its constraint, so a console created without `features` has
  // no optional method (ADR 0002).
  // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-empty-object-type
  TFeatures extends Partial<OptionalFeatures> = {}
> {
  /** The optional features; fixed for the life of the console. */
  features?: TFeatures
  commands: CommandDefinition[]
  /** The root prompt; default `'>'`. */
  prompt?: string
  /** The first value of each slice; ignored for a controlled slice. */
  initialState?: Partial<ControllableState>
  /** A slice given here is controlled (core README: Controlled slices). */
  state?: Partial<ControllableState>
  onEntriesChange?: (updater: Updater<ConsoleEntry[]>) => void
  onRecallChange?: (updater: Updater<string[]>) => void
  onContextChange?: (updater: Updater<ContextFrame[]>) => void
  /**
   * Makes the id of an entry or a run. Default: a per-console counter
   * (`c1`, `c2`, …) that skips ids already in `entries`.
   */
  createId?: () => string
  /** Drops the oldest entries beyond this; default unbounded. */
  maxEntries?: number
  /** Called when a command is about to run, with the run's signal. */
  beforeRun?: (
    info: RunInfo,
    signal: AbortSignal
  ) => BeforeRunResult | Promise<BeforeRunResult>
  /**
   * A command threw or rejected (`info` set), or a callback threw (`info`
   * null). Receives the error exactly as it was thrown.
   */
  onError?: (error: unknown, info: RunInfo | null) => void
  /** Turns a command's error into its output; default `command-failed`. */
  formatError?: (error: unknown, info: RunInfo) => CommandResponse
  /** The `close` effect. */
  onClose?: () => void
  /** Marks more lines sensitive; OR-ed with the commands' `sensitive`. */
  isSensitive?: (line: string) => boolean
  /** The most lines recall keeps (recall feature); default 100. */
  recallLimit?: number
  /** Whether a line is recorded (recall feature); default every line. */
  shouldRecord?: (line: string) => boolean
}

// packages/command-console-core/src/core/console/console.types.ts
/** A console with the core features and the optional ones in `TFeatures`. */
export type Console<
  // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-empty-object-type
  TFeatures extends Partial<OptionalFeatures> = {}
> = CoreConsoleAPI<TFeatures> & FeatureAPIsOf<TFeatures>

// packages/command-console-core/src/core/dispatch/dispatch.types.ts
/**
 * What `beforeRun` returns: `undefined` goes on to the command's `run`;
 * `false` ends the run silently; a response ends the run as if the command
 * had returned it (effects, then output).
 */
export type BeforeRunResult = undefined | false | CommandResponse

// packages/command-console-core/src/core/dispatch/dispatch.types.ts
/**
 * What the console tells its callbacks about a run. It never carries the line
 * or the arguments, for any command (P16).
 */
export interface RunInfo {
  runId: string
  /** The input entry of the line that started the run. */
  inputId: string
  /** The name as typed; `null` when the line is sensitive. */
  name: string | null
  /** The canonical name of the command. */
  command: string
  /** Whether the line was sensitive. */
  sensitive: boolean
  /** The context frames when the run started, bottom → top. */
  context: ContextFrame[]
}

// packages/command-console-core/src/core/dispatch/dispatch.types.ts
/** What a command's `run` may return. */
export type CommandReturn = void | string | OutputBlock[] | CommandResponse

// packages/command-console-core/src/core/dispatch/dispatch.types.ts
/** A command: its JSON spec plus the functions that run and complete it. */
export interface CommandDefinition extends CommandSpec {
  /**
   * Runs the command. A promise makes the run asynchronous; the console
   * stays locked until it settles or the run is cancelled.
   */
  run(
    request: CommandRequest,
    run: RunContext
  ): CommandReturn | Promise<CommandReturn>
  /**
   * The candidates for an argument (completion feature). Synchronous in 1.0.
   * Called only for safe positions (README: Completion).
   */
  complete?(request: CompletionRequest): CompletionResult
}

// packages/command-console-core/src/core/dispatch/dispatch.types.ts
/** The parsed line a command runs with. */
export interface CommandRequest {
  /** The name as typed (an alias stays an alias). */
  name: string
  /** The canonical name. */
  command: string
  /** The tokens after the name, quotes removed. */
  args: string[]
  /** The raw text after the name and the whitespace that follows it. */
  rest: string
  /** The whole line, trimmed. */
  line: string
  /** The context frames when the run started, bottom → top, root excluded. */
  context: ContextFrame[]
}

// packages/command-console-core/src/core/dispatch/dispatch.types.ts
/** The handle a running command gets. */
export interface RunContext {
  runId: string
  inputId: string
  /**
   * Aborted on cancel, `reset()`, `dispose()` and a context change made by
   * anything other than the run's own effects.
   */
  signal: AbortSignal
  /**
   * Appends an output entry for this run. Joins an open action, else is its
   * own; does nothing once the run has ended.
   */
  write(output: string | OutputBlock[], tone?: OutputEntry['tone']): void
}

// packages/command-console-core/src/core/dispatch/dispatch.types.ts
/** What a command's `complete` is asked (completion feature). */
export interface CompletionRequest {
  /** `null` while the command name is completed. */
  command: string | null
  /** The complete arguments before the one completed (safe positions only). */
  args: string[]
  /** The typed part of the token at the caret, quotes removed. */
  prefix: string
  /** The argument index completed, 0-based; -1 for the name. */
  index: number
  context: ContextFrame[]
}

// packages/command-console-core/src/core/dispatch/dispatch.types.ts
/**
 * The candidates of a `complete` call. The library filters them
 * (case-insensitive `startsWith(prefix)`). `final: false` keeps the space out
 * after a single candidate (default true).
 */
export type CompletionResult =
  string[] | { candidates: string[]; final?: boolean }

// packages/command-console-core/src/shared/keys.ts
/** A key press as the adapter reports it; core never sees a DOM event. */
export interface KeyInput {
  key: string
  ctrlKey: boolean
  shiftKey: boolean
  altKey: boolean
  metaKey: boolean
  /** A key during IME composition is never handled. */
  isComposing: boolean
  /** Whether text is selected in the input or in the console's document. */
  selection: 'none' | 'input' | 'document'
}

// packages/command-console-core/src/store/action.ts
// Updaters (core README: Controlled slices). A controlled slice is reported as
// one updater per action that replays every change of the action, in order,
// onto the value it is given.

/** A new value, or a function from the old value to the new one. */
export type Updater<T> = T | ((old: T) => T)
```

## Behavior rules

#### C-01 Plain console

`createConsole({ commands })` works with the core features only; optional feature methods are absent from the
instance and its type.

#### C-02 Features

Options merge feature defaults, then the given options; `setOptions` keeps the defaults and cannot change the feature
set.

#### C-03 Inputs never mutated

Options, `initialState`, controlled state, commands and their returns are never written; deep-frozen inputs work
through every action.

#### C-04 Controlled slices

With `state.entries` (resp. `recall`, `context`) given, the console reads the slice from options, `state` wins over
`initialState`, and each action reports its changes through one `on*Change` updater that composes them all. A value
the consumer passes back (accepted, rejected or edited) is the base of the next action.

#### C-05 Actions

Each action notifies subscribers at most once; nothing is notified or called on creation; a throwing callback does not
stop the others or the cleanup.

#### C-06 JSON

Every entry, block, response, effect and frame the console produces survives a JSON round trip and holds only finite
numbers.

#### C-07 Dispose

`dispose()` invalidates and aborts the running run, runs disposers once, clears state, and makes every later call a
no-op.

#### C-08 Isolation

Two consoles share no state, ids, DOM ids or timers; disposing one does not affect the other.

#### C-09 Submit

Enter ends the line: an input entry with the current prompt and trimmed text, then the line-end cleanup. An empty line
adds an empty input entry and nothing else.

#### C-10 Tokenizer

Whitespace (tabs included) separates; quotes group; escapes only inside `"…"`; `\` literal outside; spans cover the
raw text; nothing is dropped; `quoteArgument` round-trips.

#### C-11 Unterminated quote

Dispatch gives `unterminated-quote` and runs nothing; the tolerant tokens mark the open token.

#### C-12 Request

`run` gets one `CommandRequest` (`name`, `command`, `args`, `rest`, `line`, `context` snapshot).

#### C-13 Lookup

Only registered names and aliases run, matched exactly; a dot is an ordinary character; an unknown name gives
`command-not-found` with the first token.

#### C-14 beforeRun

Runs inside the run (read-only input, cancellable, `phase: 'authorizing'`) with `RunInfo` and the signal; `undefined`
goes on, `false` stops silently, a response is handled as the run's fulfil (effects, then output), a throw ends the run
as failed.

#### C-15 Cancel line

Ctrl+C without a selection and without a run ends the line as `cancelled` with the line-end cleanup and records
nothing.

#### C-16 Run lock

While a run exists, Enter, Tab and recall do nothing and `submit()` / `run(line)` resolve `false`; the input is
writable again after every outcome.

#### C-17 Stale runs

A settle, effect or `write` of a run that is no longer current changes nothing and calls nothing (`onError` included),
and never clears another run's `running`.

#### C-18 Errors

A throw or rejection calls `onError(error, RunInfo)` and handles `formatError`'s response as a fulfil, or appends
`command-failed` without the error's text; a throwing `formatError` falls back to the default.

#### C-19 Recall order

Unique lines oldest → newest; re-recording moves a line to the newest.

#### C-20 Recall browsing

ArrowUp keeps the draft and shows the newest, stops at the oldest; ArrowDown past the newest restores the draft; an
edit ends browsing; an external `recall` change ends browsing.

#### C-21 Recall filter

`shouldRecord` and sensitivity run before insertion; empty and cancelled lines are not recorded; unknown, unparsable
and failing lines are.

#### C-22 Recall limit

`recallLimit` drops the oldest.

#### C-23 Clear recall

`clearRecall()` and the `clear-recall` effect empty the list and end browsing in one action.

#### C-24 Initial state

`initialState` seeds `entries`, `recall`, `context` only; nothing else is added on creation.

#### C-25 Effects

Effects apply in order before the output; `clear` empties the entries; `close` calls `onClose` (Vue: the `close`
event); an effect without its feature is ignored.

#### C-26 Context stack

`push-context` / `pop-context` / `reset-context` change the stack; popping at the root does nothing; a request
carries the snapshot taken at its start.

#### C-27 Prompt snapshot

An input entry keeps the prompt it was ended with; the next prompt follows the top frame.

#### C-28 Returns

`void` gives no output entry, a string one text block, a block array those blocks, a response its output with its
`tone` and `quiet`; same content, same entries.

#### C-29 Write

`write()` appends in call order, joins an open action, and does nothing after the run ended.

#### C-30 Sensitivity

A line whose first token resolves case-insensitively, quotes removed, to a sensitive command, or that the predicate
marks (or whose predicate throws), ends as an input entry with `text: null`, `redacted: true`.

#### C-31 Redacted recall

A sensitive line is never in `recall` nor in the recall draft, in any outcome.

#### C-32 Redacted cancel

A sensitive line ended with Ctrl+C is redacted and its draft dropped.

#### C-33 Redacted messages

For a sensitive line, `command-not-found` carries `name: null` and `unterminated-quote` carries `index: null`;
`RunInfo` never carries the line or arguments.

#### C-34 No error text

The default error entry carries no part of the error.

#### C-35 Redacted completion

Positions at or after `fromArg` (all, for `sensitive: true` or a predicate match) call no provider and open no session;
safe positions get only the arguments before `fromArg`.

#### C-36 Leak matrix

For every path (submit, cancel, parse error, unknown, refusal, failure, interrupt, completion, recall draft, reset,
dispose, late rejection), the secret is absent from the state, every callback and event argument at call time
(updaters resolved, errors' own fields included), the DOM, the accessibility tree and the input element that held it.
The library never adds the line or the request to an error; an error the command itself builds is the command's.

#### C-37 Name completion

Tab on the first token completes visible names and aliases.

#### C-38 Argument completion

Tab on a later safe token asks the command's `complete` with `args`, `prefix`, `index`, `context`; no `complete`, or a
throwing one, gives no candidates.

#### C-39 No candidates

The input does not change.

#### C-40 One candidate

The candidate is written into the token's span and its quote closed, and a space is added unless `final: false`, the
token is not the last, or a space already follows it; the caret follows it. Quoting: a quoted or open token keeps its
quote character, except that `'…'` becomes `"…"` for a candidate containing `'`; a bare token whose text needs quoting
(`quoteArgument(text) !== text`) opens `'`, or `"` when the text contains `'`.

#### C-41 Several candidates

The longest common prefix is written when longer than the typed prefix, without closing a quote; the list opens;
Tab/ArrowDown and Shift+Tab/ArrowUp select with wrap and write the candidate into the span; text outside the span is
kept; Enter on a selection accepts it as C-40 does and submits nothing; Escape restores the original token.

#### C-42 (withdrawn)

Async completion is not in 1.0 (README, "Not in 1.0").

#### C-43 Completion closes

An edit or caret move the session did not make closes the session and keeps the text; tolerant tokens complete inside
an open quote, keeping its quote character.

#### C-44 Busy (Vue)

While a run exists the root has `data-busy`, the status element shows `labels.busy` (or the `busy` slot) and the input
is `readonly`; the log has no `aria-busy`.

#### C-45 DOM contract (Vue)

The elements the library renders carry only the classes, attributes and ids of `contract/dom.ts`, each on the element
it is listed for; slot content is excluded.

#### C-46 No styles (Vue)

No element the library renders has a `style` attribute; no size or `overflow` is set.

#### C-47 Labels (Vue)

Every text comes from `labels`; no literal `aria-label` in a `.vue` file; message codes render through
`labels.messages`; a partial `labels.messages` keeps the other defaults.

#### C-48 Accessibility (Vue)

axe-core finds no violation with the list closed and open; the log is a named `role="log"`; the input is a named and
described combobox with `aria-controls` and `aria-activedescendant` only when they point to existing elements; the
listbox is named; a recalled line is written to the status element; quiet entries are `aria-live="off"`.

#### C-49 Packaging

ESM only, own `.d.ts`, `vue` a peer, no alias or `optimizeDeps` needed by a consumer, `README.md` and `LICENSE.md` in
every tarball (pack-install test).

#### C-50 No transport, no storage

No package reads or writes storage or the network.

#### C-51 Focus (Vue)

`autofocus` focuses on mount; a click anywhere in the console (the log, the status, the completion list, the input
line and the empty space around them) focuses the input unless text is selected or the target is interactive.

#### C-52 Keys scoped (Vue)

Keys are handled on the input only; no listener remains after unmount; Ctrl+C with a selection is not prevented.

#### C-53 Key map

The fixed key map (the table above; README, "Keyboard") applies with exact modifiers; a key with `isComposing` is never handled.

#### C-54 Input replaced (Vue)

After a sensitive line ends, after `reset()` and after any programmatic clear of a non-empty input, the input is a new
element (identity check) with an empty value; it has focus only if the old one had it. A native undo
(`execCommand('undo')`) in the new element brings nothing back.

#### C-55 maxEntries and ids

Appending beyond `maxEntries` drops the oldest in the same action; generated ids skip existing ones; appending a
duplicate id throws.

#### C-56 Command names

Invalid or duplicate names and aliases, and an invalid `fromArg`, throw at creation and at `setOptions`.

#### C-57 Interrupt

Ctrl+C or `cancel()` during a run invalidates the run, then aborts its signal, then appends `interrupted`; the run's
cleanup runs once.

#### C-58 Scroll (Vue)

The log sticks to the bottom only while it is at the bottom and after the user's own submit; `scrollTop` is the only
style-related write; the `ResizeObserver` is disconnected on unmount and its late callback does nothing.

#### C-59 Focus exit (Vue)

Tab on an empty input and Shift+Tab without a session are not prevented, so focus leaves the console.

#### C-60 Nested actions

Method calls and `write()` inside an open action join it: two synchronous `write()` calls in `run` followed by a
return give one notification, with the input entry and the three outputs in order.

#### C-61 Same-tick updates

Two actions in one tick without a `setOptions` in between build on the last reported value; a value passed back with
`setOptions` wins over it. Tested in core and through `v-model` in Vue.

#### C-62 External context change

A change of the context during a run by anything other than the run's own effects (a context method call, an external
controlled `context`) aborts the run's signal and drops its context effects; its output still appears.

#### C-63 run and submit

`submit()` ends the live input as Enter does; `run(line)` replaces the live input with `line` (incrementing
`input.revision` when it was not empty) and submits it; both resolve `true` after the run's end action, or after the
line ended when nothing ran, and `false` when a run already exists.

#### C-64 submit event (Vue)

The `submit` event carries only `{ inputId, sensitive }`.

#### C-65 getCommands

`getCommands()` lists the specs that are not `hidden`, in registration order, each with its aliases.

#### C-66 Context depth (Vue)

The root's `data-context-depth` equals the number of context frames after every action.

#### C-67 Slots (Vue)

A `block-<type>` slot replaces the rendering of that block type only; `prompt`, `busy` and `completion` render inside
their library element, which keeps its classes, ids and ARIA attributes.

#### C-68 Composable (Vue)

`useCommandConsole` passes reactive option changes to `setOptions`, mirrors every notification into its `state`, does
no DOM work, and disposes the console when its effect scope is disposed.

#### C-69 No form, no name (Vue)

The input is not inside a `<form>` rendered by the library and has no `name` attribute; `autocomplete`,
`autocorrect`, `autocapitalize` and `spellcheck` are off.

## DOM contract

The classes and attributes below are the only hooks a skin can select (P6). The console writes no stylesheet and no inline style (P5); slot content is the consumer’s.

### Classes

| Class | Element | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cc-console` | `div` | Root element. It sets no size and no `overflow`: the consumer’s CSS gives it its size (P13). |
| `cc-log` | `.cc-console > div` | The scrollback, a named `role="log"`. Make it scroll in your CSS (`overflow-y: auto` and a height); the console only writes its `scrollTop` to keep the newest output in view (C-58). |
| `cc-entries` | `.cc-log > div` | The list of entries inside the log, observed for size changes to keep the log at the bottom (C-58). |
| `cc-entry` | `.cc-entries > div` | One entry: an ended input line or the output of a command (`data-kind`). |
| `cc-prompt` | `span` | The prompt, in an input entry and before the live input. The `prompt` slot renders inside it (C-67). |
| `cc-line` | `.cc-entry > span` | The text of an ended input line, or `labels.redacted` when the line was sensitive (C-30). |
| `cc-cancelled` | `.cc-entry > span` | After a line ended with Ctrl+C: `labels.cancelledMarker` (C-15). |
| `cc-block` | `.cc-entry > *` | One output block (`data-type`): `pre` for text, JSON and custom blocks, `table` for a table, `ul` for a list, `div` for a message. A `block-<type>` slot replaces its content (C-67). |
| `cc-status` | `.cc-console > div` | A `role="status"` element: `labels.busy` (or the `busy` slot) while a command runs, the recalled line after a recall, else empty (C-44, C-48). |
| `cc-completions` | `.cc-console > ul` | The completion candidates, a named `role="listbox"`, rendered only while a completion session is open (C-41). |
| `cc-completion` | `.cc-completions > li` | One candidate, a `role="option"`. The `completion` slot renders inside it (C-67). |
| `cc-input-line` | `.cc-console > div` | The live line: its prompt and the input. Never a `<form>` (C-69). |
| `cc-input` | `input` | The text input, a named and described combobox. It is replaced by a new element after a sensitive line, on `reset()` and after a programmatic clear (C-54). |

### Attributes

| Attribute | Element | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `data-busy` | `.cc-console` | Present while a command runs (C-44). |
| `data-context-depth` | `.cc-console` | The number of context frames, `0` at the root (C-66). A skin may change the look of a nested context with it. |
| `role` | `.cc-log, .cc-status, .cc-completions, .cc-completion, .cc-input` | `log` on the log, `status` on the status element, `listbox` on the list, `option` on a candidate, `combobox` on the input (C-48). |
| `aria-label` | `.cc-log, .cc-completions, .cc-input` | From `labels.log`, `labels.completions` and `labels.input` (C-47). |
| `data-kind` | `.cc-entry` | `input` for an ended line, `output` for what a command returned. |
| `data-tone` | `.cc-entry` | The tone of an output entry as the command gave it (for example an error), for the skin to colour. |
| `data-status` | `.cc-entry` | How an input line ended (for example `cancelled` or `failed`), for the skin to mark it. |
| `data-redacted` | `.cc-entry` | Present on the input entry of a sensitive line, whose text is not kept (C-30). |
| `aria-live` | `.cc-entry` | `off` on a quiet entry, which the log does not announce (C-48). |
| `data-type` | `.cc-block` | The block type: `text`, `json`, `table`, `list`, `message` or `custom`. |
| `scope` | `.cc-block th` | `col` on each header cell of a table block. |
| `id` | `.cc-completions, .cc-completion` | From Vue’s `useId()`: the list id, and `<list id>-<n>` per candidate, unique per console (C-08). |
| `aria-selected` | `.cc-completion` | `true` on the selected candidate, `false` on the others. |
| `type` | `.cc-input` | `text`. |
| `aria-autocomplete` | `.cc-input` | `list`. |
| `aria-expanded` | `.cc-input` | `true` while the completion list is open, else `false`. |
| `aria-controls` | `.cc-input` | The list id, only while the list is open (C-48). |
| `aria-activedescendant` | `.cc-input` | The id of the selected candidate, only while one is selected (C-48). |
| `aria-description` | `.cc-input` | From `labels.inputDescription`: how Enter and Tab behave, including that Tab on an empty line leaves the console (C-59). |
| `autocomplete` | `.cc-input` | `off` (C-69). |
| `autocorrect` | `.cc-input` | `off` (C-69). |
| `autocapitalize` | `.cc-input` | `off` (C-69). |
| `spellcheck` | `.cc-input` | `false` (C-69). |
| `readonly` | `.cc-input` | Present while a command runs (C-16, C-44). |

## How the contract is kept

- `pnpm contract:check` regenerates this file and fails if it differs, so the component, `packages/command-console/src/contract.ts`, the rules and the DOM list cannot change without it.
- `pnpm api:check` compares the built declarations of each package with its `etc/*.api.md` report.
- `pnpm contract:gen` also checks that the props, events, slots and exposed keys of the component equal those of `packages/command-console/src/contract.ts`.
- `tests/repo/contract-traceability.spec.ts` fails when a rule has no test named after it, or a test names an unknown or withdrawn rule. That is traceability, not coverage: it does not say the test proves the rule.
- The browser tests compare the rendered DOM with the DOM contract (C-45).
